title: HW topology-aware kernel selector and prefill/decode packetizer for MIG & clock domains
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We observe tail latency and throughput regressions on multi-tenant nodes where different MIG shapes and clock states co-exist. Current kernel selection is static per-model and does not consider (a) MIG instance size, (b) active GPU clock governor, or (c) co-located workload packing. That leads to suboptimal kernel dispatch (e.g., using low-memory but high-latency matmul kernels) and increased 99th-percentile decode latency during prefill spikes.

Goal: Build a topology-aware runtime component (kernel selector + packetizer) that: (1) introspects the local GPU topology and MIG partitions, (2) observes current clock domains and power caps, (3) decides kernel variants and prefill/decode packetization that maximize throughput under SLOs, and (4) exposes a safefallback to conservative kernels when telemetry is noisy. Target KPIs: reduce p99 decode latency by >=12% on mixed MIG workloads, increase steady-state throughput 6-10% for long-sequence workloads, and lower per-token GPU cost by ~7% at 95% utilization.

Scope: H100 and A10 primary targets; L40S smoke-tested (no MIG). Implementation will be in serving-runtime (C++ kernel registry + scheduler hooks) with a small control-plane service for topology policy rules and an opt-in runtime flag.

Acceptance criteria: (1) Kernel selector that chooses kernels based on MIG shape and current clock state for sample models (gpt-2-small, rlhf-7b, and a 70B distil test model). (2) Packetizer that groups prefill tokens across compatible requests to improve kernel utilization without violating latency SLOs. (3) Integration tests that simulate heterogeneous co-tenancy and validate no increase in error rates. (4) Benchmark dashboard showing KPI improvements vs baseline.

Implementation notes and decisions:
- Kernel registry extended with metadata: supported_mig_shapes (string tag), min_clock_state, memory_overhead_estimate. This allows fast filtering at dispatch time.
- Packetizer uses a timebox-based gather window (default 2ms) with a dynamic backoff when p99 approaches SLO. This trades micro-latency for throughput in a controlled way.
- We avoid model-specific heuristics; instead we index by model-shape and observed per-step memory footprint to ensure generality.
- Clock telemetry: we sample nvml clocks and ration by flavor (performance vs eco). If clock changes mid-request, runtime re-evaluates kernel choice and may fall back to conservative decode path.

Bench plan and datasets:
- Microbench: single-instance MIG shapes (1g.10g, 2g.20g equivalents) for H100 using internal perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/734
- Mixed-tenancy: synthetic mix of short-chat and long-generation flows with controlled concurrency and power caps.
- Real traffic replay: 24-hour replay from a dedicated customer staging cluster (anonymized): S3 path in attachments.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag "hw_topo_packetizer=true". Canary rollout to 5 Dedicated nodes (H100) for 72h, monitor p50/p90/p99, GPU occupancy, and error counts. If p99 regresses >5% or OOMs observed, automatic rollback.

Observability: add the following metrics: selected_kernel_id, packetizer_window_ms, packets_merged, fallback_reason, clock_state_at_dispatch. Hook these to runtime dashboards and alert when fallback_ratio > 1%.

Links: Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/123456789/HW+Topo+Kernel+Selector, Perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/734, Runtime PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2091, Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/abc123/hw-topo-packetizer
acceptance_criteria: Selector picks kernel variant matching MIG shape and clock for sample models (gpt-2-small, rlhf-7b, 70B) in microbench
Packetizer merges prefill tokens without p90 exceeding SLO in canary runs
No increase in OOM or error rates across integration tests
Bench dashboard shows p99 decode latency reduction >=12% for mixed MIG workloads

steps: 1) Finalize kernel registry metadata and land schema migration (runtime PR)
2) Implement packetizer gather window and dynamic backoff logic
3) Add nvml clock sampling & dispatch re-eval hook
4) Run microbench on H100/A10/L40S and populate bench dashboard
5) Canary on Dedicated H100 nodes for 72h, monitor metrics and auto-rollback conditions
6) Postmortem + playbook for customer escalations and rollback
risks_mitigation: Risk: mid-request clock changes cause instability -> Mitigation: re-eval kernel choice and switch to conservative decode path under safe-guard timebox
Risk: packetizer increases tail latency -> Mitigation: dynamic backoff when p99 approaches SLO and telemetry-based undo
Risk: MIG shape misclassification -> Mitigation: cross-check nvml topology and heuristic fallback to memory-centric kernel
